paragraphs.title: Opening of the Psalm: An Address to All People

answers: Only to kings
To all people and all inhabitants of the world
Only to the sons of Korah
easy.explanation: The psalmist calls all people and all inhabitants of the world to hear.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist speak at the beginning?

answers: Both low and high, rich and poor
Only the wise
Only soldiers
easy.explanation: The verse names both low and high, rich and poor.
easy.q: Which groups of people are mentioned together?

answers: A military battle
The praise of riches
Wisdom and understanding
easy.explanation: His mouth will speak of wisdom, and his heart will meditate on understanding.
easy.q: What will the psalmist speak about?

answers: Because the message is intended for people of every class
Because only poor people understand riddles
Because he speaks only about his family
medium.explanation: The opening presents the message as relevant to all people, regardless of status.
medium.q: Why is the psalmist's address to all people appropriate to the passage?

answers: By means of a law and a commandment
Through a parable and a dark saying upon the harp
Through prayer only
medium.explanation: He will incline his ear to a parable and open his dark saying upon the harp.
medium.q: How does the psalmist describe the way he will present his message?

answers: A difficult or mysterious saying requiring thought
The house where he lives
The wealth he has gathered
medium.explanation: A dark saying is a profound or mysterious statement that requires understanding.
medium.q: What does “dark saying” mean in this context?

answers: The psalmist separates people into classes
The psalmist includes different groups together
The psalmist is speaking about only two people
challenge.explanation: The pairings show that the message includes people of every rank and economic condition.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated pairing of different groups of people?

answers: The wisdom deserves careful attention and reflection
The wisdom is presented as unimportant
The wisdom is intended only for harp players
challenge.explanation: The psalmist calls people to hear because his message requires attention and understanding.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the call to listen and the wisdom being presented?

answers: Day and night
Wisdom and music
Rich and poor
challenge.explanation: The opening expressly joins the rich and poor in one audience.
challenge.q: Which contrast is already emphasized in the opening?

short_answers.question: What should the inhabitants of the world do according to verse 1?
short_answers.answer: They should give ear and listen.
short_answers.explanation: The psalmist commands all inhabitants of the world to hear.

short_answers.question: What will the meditation of the psalmist's heart be about?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 3 says that the meditation of his heart shall be of understanding.

short_answers.question: What instrument is mentioned in connection with the dark saying?
short_answers.explanation: The psalmist says he will open his dark saying upon the harp.

paragraphs.title: Wealth Cannot Save a Person from Death

answers: People who trust in their riches and boast in their abundance
People who trust only in wisdom
People who depend on their friends
easy.explanation: The passage describes those who trust in their wealth and boast in the multitude of their riches.
easy.q: What kind of people are described as trusting in their wealth?

answers: A house
A ransom
A song
easy.explanation: No person can give God a ransom for his brother.
easy.q: What can no person give to God for another person's soul?

answers: It remains in their hands
It disappears immediately
They leave it to others
easy.explanation: The wise, foolish, and brutish all perish and leave their wealth to others.
easy.q: What happens to the wealth of people when they die?

answers: No one can pay God a sufficient ransom
Wealth always goes only to the poor
People have no possessions during life
medium.explanation: The passage says that none can redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him.
medium.q: Why can wealth not redeem a person's life?

answers: A dwelling place
A payment for release
A person's name
medium.explanation: A ransom is a payment intended to secure a person's release or redemption.
medium.q: What does “ransom” mean in this passage?

answers: Death comes even to those who possess great riches
Wealth prevents every person from dying
Only poor people die
medium.explanation: The passage shows that rich people also perish, so wealth cannot ultimately protect them.
medium.q: How does death strengthen the argument against trusting in wealth?

answers: Both show that wealth cannot control a person's fate after death
Both prove that the rich live forever
Both describe the success of a ransom
challenge.explanation: A person cannot purchase escape from death, and after death his possessions pass to others.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the inability to pay a ransom and leaving wealth to others?

answers: To say that only wise people will be saved
To show that death reaches people of different kinds
To distinguish only between rich and poor
challenge.explanation: The various groups are all said to perish, emphasizing the universality of death.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention wise men, fools, and brutish persons together?

answers: Human redemption by wealth is permanently beyond reach
Redemption happens every day
Wealth continually increases
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the required ransom cannot be provided by human beings.
challenge.q: What does “it ceaseth for ever” suggest about redemption?

short_answers.question: What do the wealthy boast in?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 6 says they boast themselves in the multitude of their riches.

short_answers.question: Whom can no person redeem by his own means?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 7 says that none can by any means redeem his brother.

short_answers.question: To whom do people leave their wealth when they perish?
short_answers.explanation: The passage says they perish and leave their wealth to others.

paragraphs.title: The Futility of Earthly Honor and the Descent to the Grave

answers: That they will continue for ever
That they are worthless during life
That they belong only to strangers
easy.explanation: Their inward thought is that their houses will continue for ever and to all generations.
easy.q: What do people imagine about their houses and dwelling places?

answers: Kings in palaces
Sheep
Birds
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Like sheep they are laid in the grave.”
easy.q: To what are people compared when they are laid in the grave?

answers: It grows stronger
It remains unchanged
It is consumed
easy.explanation: Their beauty shall consume in the grave.
easy.q: What happens to their beauty in the grave?

answers: They expect lasting homes, but they are laid in the grave
They expect poverty, but become rich
They desire wisdom, but become musicians
medium.explanation: They imagine permanent houses and names, yet their mortal destiny is the grave.
medium.q: What is the central contrast between people's expectations and their destiny?

answers: Does not remain
Wins a victory
Is preserved forever
medium.explanation: The phrase means that a person does not remain permanently in earthly honor.
medium.q: What does “abideth not” mean in “man being in honour abideth not”?

answers: The dead build houses
The upright have dominion over them
The wealthy return to their possessions
medium.explanation: The upright shall have dominion over those in the grave in the morning.
medium.q: What happens in the morning according to verse 14?

answers: Even those with names and possessions are eventually laid in the grave
People are forbidden to use names
The lands become wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage shows that earthly names and possessions do not prevent death.
challenge.q: Why does having a name for one's lands not guarantee lasting existence?

answers: People are led toward death without being able to stop it
People live in abundance and safety
People become shepherds
challenge.explanation: The comparison presents people as being brought to the grave like sheep.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to sheep convey about human destiny?

answers: It emphasizes that human honor does not last
It proves that houses remain forever
It describes a night of celebration
challenge.explanation: The phrase directly states that a person does not remain permanently in earthly honor.
challenge.q: How does “abideth not” support the message about earthly honor?

short_answers.question: What do people call their lands after?
short_answers.explanation: They call their lands after their own names.

short_answers.question: What happens to man who is in honour?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says that man being in honour does not remain.

short_answers.question: Who shall have dominion in the morning?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 14 says that the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning.

paragraphs.title: Hope in God and the Choice of Goodness

answers: Wealth
The person himself
God
easy.explanation: The psalmist declares that God will redeem his soul from the power of the grave.
easy.q: Who can redeem the psalmist's soul from the power of the grave?

answers: When a person is made rich and his house is increased in glory
Listening to wisdom
Doing what is good
easy.explanation: He says, “Be not thou afraid when one is made rich.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say not to fear?

answers: It descends with him forever
It does not go with him
It becomes greater
easy.explanation: His glory shall not descend after him.
easy.q: What happens to a person's glory when he dies?

answers: Earthly wealth and glory do not continue after death
The rich person has no house during life
The rich person is always poor
medium.explanation: When the rich person dies, he carries nothing away and his glory does not follow him.
medium.q: Why should a person not envy someone who is rich and honored?

answers: To rescue or deliver
To praise
To conceal
medium.explanation: Here redeem means to rescue the soul from the power of the grave.
medium.q: What does “redeem” mean in “God will redeem my soul”?

answers: He blesses his soul in life, but afterward goes to the generation of his fathers
He is poor in life, but becomes rich after death
He is in the grave during life, but returns to his house afterward
medium.explanation: The passage describes a person praising himself in life but ultimately going to his fathers and not seeing light.
medium.q: What contrast is made between a person's life and his final destiny?

answers: They rely on temporary riches, while he relies on God's redemption
They trust in God, while he trusts only in money
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts confidence in wealth with confidence in God's power to redeem.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between those who trust in wealth and the psalmist's hope?

answers: True value should not depend on temporary earthly honor
Earthly glory is the only thing that remains
A person can purchase eternal life
challenge.explanation: The warning distinguishes temporary honor from what has lasting spiritual importance.
challenge.q: What does the repeated warning that glory does not follow a person imply?

answers: Both concern listening to a particular king
Both emphasize the difference between wisdom and failure to understand
Both describe the building of houses
challenge.explanation: The psalm opens with wisdom and ends by warning against failing to understand the temporary nature of honor.
challenge.q: How does the end of the psalm connect with its opening?

short_answers.question: What will God redeem according to verse 15?
short_answers.answer: The psalmist's soul from the power of the grave.
short_answers.explanation: God will redeem the psalmist's soul from the power of the grave.

short_answers.question: What will a person carry away when he dies?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 17 says that when he dies he shall carry nothing away.

short_answers.question: What will the person in honour be like if he understandeth not?
short_answers.explanation: The final verse compares the person who lacks understanding to beasts that perish.
